# Volume 2 — XVI The Substance of Things Hoped For

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Nell,” Robin pleaded, climbing onto the polished, leather-upholstered couch inside the Grey Shutters kitchen, where Nell was seated, going through a letter, “Nell, I’m awful hungry. You’ve no idea.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0000 }

“In a moment, I will fetch a slice of bread and butter for you,” Nell said distractedly. Some thrilling news was clearly in her letter, because her cheeks matched the pink of the roses growing on the large exterior bush, and her eyes shone with a star-like quality that belonged uniquely to Nell.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0001 }

“However, bread and butter is not what I am hungry for,” Robin stated, sounding repulsed. “Plum cake is what I am hungry for.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0002 }

“Oh,” Nell chuckled, setting her letter aside and wrapping her arm around Robin to press him close, “that sort of appetite can be borne quite easily, Robin-boy. You are aware that Thirza has a rule stating you may only eat bread and butter in between meals.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0003 }

“Well, pass me a portion then . . . if you would.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0004 }

It was finally instilled in Robin to utter “please,” yet he usually added it as an appended thought. He observed with favor the ample piece that Nell soon carried over to him. “You always put such a nice lot of butter on it, Nell. Thirza spreads it pretty thin. It slips down a lot easier when there’s plenty of butter.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0005 }

Based on the speed with which it vanished, the piece seemed to "slip down" fairly easily. Slipping head foremost off the couch, Robin completed two somersaults upon the rug before sitting upright and stating with certainty,
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0006 }

“Nell, concerning heaven, my mind is made up; going there is not what I want.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0007 }

“Why not?” asked Nell gravely.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0008 }

“Because paradise resides in the attic of Simon Fletcher, and Simon Fletcher is not to my liking.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0009 }

“Heaven in . . . Simon Fletcher’s garret!” sputtered Nell, far too astounded to even laugh. “Robin Farrow, what could have possibly driven such a bizarre thought into your mind?”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0010 }

“That is the location, according to Milty Gammon. It happened this past Sunday during Sunday School. Elijah and Elisha were the subjects of the lesson, and I spoke up to ask Miss Rogerson where heaven was located. Miss Rogerson appeared extremely offended. She was already angry, since Milty Gammon had answered ‘His old clo’es,’ when she queried us about what Elijah bequeathed to Elisha upon ascending to heaven, and we boys all chuckled before thinking. I desire that one could think prior to acting, since you then would refrain from doing those things. However, disrespect was not Milty’s intention. The name of the object simply escaped his mind. Miss Rogerson stated that heaven was where God resided and instructed me not to pose questions of that nature. Milty poked me with his elbow and whispered, ‘Heaven’s in Uncle Simon’s garret and I’ll esplain about it on the road home.’ Therefore, he provided an esplantation while we were returning home. Milty excels at esplaining matters. Should he lack knowledge regarding a topic, he will invent a great deal of material, allowing you to have it esplained regardless. His mother is the sister of Mrs. Simon, and he accompanied her to the funeral following the death of his cousin, Odette Harriet. The clergyman declared that she had departed to heaven, even though Milty claims her body was resting right in front of them within the coffin. Nevertheless, he presumed they transported the coffin to the garret subsequently. Now, when Milty and his mother proceeded upstairs to retrieve her bonnet once everything had concluded, he inquired of her where the heaven was that Odette Harriet had departed to, and she indicated the ceiling directly, saying, ‘Up there.’ Milty was aware that nothing existed above the ceiling except the garret, which is how he discovered it. Consequently, he has been terribly frightened to visit his Uncle Simon’s from that time forward.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0011 }

Nell placed Robin on her lap and tried her hardest to resolve this religious confusion as well. She possessed far greater ability for the job than Thirza did, because she recalled her own early years and possessed a natural grasp of the odd notions that children of seven years old occasionally form regarding subjects that are, naturally, extremely clear and easy for adults. She had only just managed to persuade Robin that heaven was not located in Simon Fletcher’s garret when Thirza arrived inside from the garden, where she had been gathering peas alongside Lucy. Lucy was a hard-working little girl who was at her contentest when “helping” with different tiny chores fitted to her plump fingers. She provided food for chickens, gathered chips, dried dishes, and went on many errands. Being tidy, dependable, and perceptive, she did not require instructions on doing a task more than once and failed to remember none of her small responsibilities. Robin, in contrast, was somewhat careless and prone to forgetting; nevertheless, he possessed a natural gift for capturing affection, and Nell and Thirza still preferred him even now.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0012 }

As Lucy proudly removed the peas from their shells and Robin constructed vessels out of the pods, complete with matchstick masts and paper sails, Nell recounted the amazing news in her letter to Thirza.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0013 }

“Oh, Thirza, what do you think? Honora wrote to me, stating that Mrs. Varley has arrived on the Island, and provided the weather is nice Thursday, their plan is to drive up to Brierley, arriving here around twelve. After spending the afternoon with us, they will head to the hotel at Pale Sands for the evening, as a few of Mrs. Varley’s American friends are residing there. Oh, Thirza, isn’t it wonderful? It barely feels real to me.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0014 }

“I suppose Mrs. Varley resembles many other folk,” Thirza remarked dryly, despite experiencing a small thrill of excitement herself. Since Mrs. Varley was a renowned lady, receiving a call from her was by no means a frequent event. “Will they be arriving for dinner, in that case?”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0015 }

“Yes; and oh, Thirza, can I prepare all of the dinner on my own? I wish to know that I am able to do a thing for the writer of ‘The Rosebud Garden,’ even if it is merely preparing a dinner for her. You won't object, will you?”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0016 }

“Heavens, I do not enjoy slaving over a warm stove in July so much that having another person take over would bother me greatly. The task is all yours.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0017 }

“Oh, thank you,” remarked Nell, as though a immense kindness had just been bestowed by Thirza, “this exact evening, I will prepare the menu.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0018 }

“It would be wise if you refrained from attempting anything excessively grand,” cautioned Thirza, who felt a slight apprehension at the elevated tone of ‘menu.’ “Failure will probably be your lot if you attempt it.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0019 }

“Oh, I am not planning to adopt any ‘style,’ if that implies attempting to perform or possess items that we do not typically possess during celebrations,” Nell promised. “Such behavior would be pretending, and, even though I realize I lack the wisdom and composure that a seventeen-year-old female and a teacher should possess, I am not that foolish. However, my desire is for every single thing to be as lovely and delicate as it can be. Robin-boy, refrain from leaving those peapods on the back stairs . . . a person could lose their footing on them. A light soup will be my first course . . . you are aware that I am capable of preparing delicious cream-of-onion soup . . . followed by a pair of roast fowls. The two white roosters will be my choice. I feel genuine fondness for those roosters, and they have been beloved companions from the moment the gray hen hatched only the two of them . . . tiny spheres of yellow fluff. Nevertheless, I am aware that their slaughter would be required eventually, and certainly no occasion could be more deserving than this one. Yet oh, Thirza, I am unable to slaughter them . . . not even on account of Mrs. Varley. John Henry Carter will have to be asked by me to travel here and perform it on my behalf.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0020 }

“I’ll manage it,” offered Robin, “provided Thirza holds onto their legs, since I reckon my two hands will be needed for the axe. Seeing them jump around once their heads are severed is terribly good fun.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0021 }

“Then as far as vegetables go, I’m going to have peas and beans and creamed potatoes and a lettuce salad,” Nell continued, “and lemon pie topped with whipped cream, alongside coffee and cheese and lady fingers for dessert. Tomorrow I will prepare the lady fingers and the pies, and I'll launder my white muslin dress. Tonight I also have to inform Isolde, because she is going to want to wash her dress. White muslin is what Mrs. Varley’s heroines almost always wear, so Isolde and I always decided that we would wear white muslin as well if we ever encountered her. Don't you agree that it will be a really delicate compliment? You cannot push peapods into the cracks in the floor, Robin, dear. Since they are all extremely eager to meet Mrs. Varley, I must invite Mr. and Mrs. Wace and Miss Thorne to dinner as well. Her arrival while Miss Thorne is visiting is so lucky. Robin dear, stop sailing the peapods inside the water bucket . . . head outside to the trough. Oh, I really hope Thursday is nice weather, and my guess is that it will be, because Uncle Zeb mentioned last night when he visited Mr. Pettifer’s house that the majority of this week would see rain.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0022 }

“That’s a favorable indication,” Thirza concurred.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0023 }

That evening, Nell sprinted over to Pear Hill to share the updates with Isolde, who shared her intense excitement, and the pair conversed about the situation while sitting in the hammock hung beneath the large willow tree located in the Pembroke garden.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0024 }

“Oh, Nell, can’t I assist you in preparing the meal?” begged Isolde. “You are aware that I am able to create wonderful lettuce salad.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0025 }

“You certainly can,” Nell generously agreed. “Furthermore, I will require your assistance with the decorations as well. My intention is to turn the parlor into a virtual arbor of flowers . . . while wild roses are meant to ornament the dining table. Oh, I truly wish that no problems arise. The lead female characters created by Mrs. Varley avoid getting into trouble or being caught unprepared, and they constantly maintain their composure alongside being such capable housekeepers. Excellent housekeeping skills appear to be inherent to them. You surely recall that Edith from ‘Edgewood Days’ managed the home for her parent at merely eight years of age. At the age of eight, I was scarcely capable of doing anything besides raising children. Having authored so many works concerning girls, Mrs. Varley ought to be an expert on the subject, and I am very eager for her to think highly of us. My mind has pictured the scenario in twelve distinct manners . . . her appearance, her remarks, and my own responses. Moreover, my nose is causing me great concern. As is visible to you, seven freckles are located upon it. Their appearance resulted from the A.V.I S. picnic, during which I walked about in the sunlight lacking my hat. Worrying about them is likely unappreciative on my part, whereas I ought to feel grateful that my entire face is not covered by them as was previously the case; nevertheless, I really prefer that they had not appeared . . . every single heroine of Mrs. Varley possesses a flawless skin tone. I am unable to remember a single one among them who had freckles.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0026 }

“The ones you have aren't particularly prominent,” Isolde offered by way of comfort. “Apply some lemon juice to them this evening.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0027 }

On the following day, Nell baked her lady fingers and pies, laundered her muslin dress, and cleaned all the rooms in the dwelling by sweeping and dusting them . . . an action that was completely uncalled for, since Grey Shutters possessed its customary immaculate condition beloved by Thirza. Nevertheless, Nell believed that even a speck of dust would desecrate a residence about to be graced by the presence of Charlotte E. Varley. She went so far as to tidy the "catch-all" cupboard beneath the staircase, despite the fact that Mrs. Varley had no chance whatsoever of viewing what was inside it.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0028 }

“However, I desire to be certain that it is in flawless condition, regardless of whether she sees it,” Nell remarked to Thirza. “As you are aware, within her volume ‘Golden Keys,’ she has her couple of heroines Alice and Louisa adopt as their slogan that stanza by Longfellow,
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0029 }

“In art’s ancient times, craftspeople labored with the utmost precision on every tiny, hidden detail, since the divine beings observe all places,”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0030 }

and in this way their basement steps were continually washed by them, and sweeping beneath the bedsteads was never overlooked. My conscience would trouble me were I to believe this cupboard was messy while Mrs. Varley remained inside the dwelling. From the time we perused ‘Golden Keys,’ this past April, that stanza has likewise been adopted as a maxim by Isolde and me.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0031 }

During that night, John Henry Carter collaborated with Robin to kill the two white roosters, after which Nell prepared them for cooking, a chore she typically disliked that was transformed into a noble endeavor because of where the well-fed fowl were headed.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0032 }

“I dislike plucking poultry,” she remarked to Thirza, “yet is it not lucky that we are not required to place our spirits into whatever task our hands happen to perform? My hands have been plucking chickens, but my mind has been wandering through the Milky Way.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0033 }

“It seemed to me that you had littered the floor with a greater number of feathers than customary,” observed Thirza.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0034 }

Afterward, Robin was put to bed by Nell, who got him to pledge that his behavior during the following day would be flawless.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0035 }

“Will you allow me to be as wicked as I please the following day, provided that I am as exceptionally well-behaved as possible throughout the entire day tomorrow?” Robin inquired.
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0036 }

“That is impossible for me,” Nell remarked in a low voice, “however, I will row you and Lucy in the punt clear to the end of the pond, where we can land upon the dunes and enjoy a picnic.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0037 }

“It’s a bargain,” declared Robin. “I’ll be good, you bet. My intention was to head to Mr. Pettifer’s to shoot peas at Nutmeg using my new popgun, yet another day will work fine. I espect it will resemble Sunday, though having a picnic at the shore will compensate for it.”
{: #nw-v02-c16-p0038 }
